content:
Public bodies spent a considerable £3.4 billion on private consultants last year, according to newly released data. This amount reflects a large increase from 2019-20, and spending has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. The surge presents a challenge for the current government, which intends to lower this spending. Recent contracts, including one with KPMG to train civil servants, have been awarded. An expert called the situation "scandalous," arguing that consultants offer little real value.
